title: Colossal magnetostriction effect in rare-earth orthoferrites
authors: Moumita Das, Arup Ghosh, Moumita Nandi, Arumugam Thamizhavel, Dipten Bhattacharya, Prabhat Mandal
abstract: Within the entire gamut of magnetostrictive, piezomagnetic, and ferromagnetic shape memory alloy systems, the striction effect is found to vary from a few tens of parts per million to a few percent. Here, we report the observation of an unprecedentedly large magnetic-field-induced lattice strain along the $c$ axis (more than 60-100% at 90 kOe field) in single crystals of orthorhombic $R$FeO$_3$ ($R$ = Dy, Ho) below their spin-reorientation transition temperature $T_{SR}$. However, the striction effect is two orders of magnitude smaller along the $a$ and $b$ axes. Like magnetostriction, the magnetodielectric effect is highly anisotropic and very large along the $c$ axis. Such gigantic striction and dielectric effects along the $c$ axis arise as a result of a magnetic-field-induced first-order structural phase transition which possibly stems from large spin-orbit coupling (and, thereby, enormous magnetocrystalline anisotropy). The observed colossal striction in rare-earth orthoferrites could open new opportunities for applications requiring large, reversible magnetic-field-induced strain.
summary: This work reports the observation of colossal, highly anisotropic magnetostriction in rare-earth orthoferrites ($	ext{RFeO}_3$). The massive lattice strain, exceeding 100% along the c-axis, is directly linked to a magnetic-field-induced first-order structural phase transition occurring below the spin-reorientation temperature. These findings suggest that $	ext{RFeO}_3$ materials are excellent candidates for applications requiring large, reversible strain control via magnetic fields.
main_problem: The study investigates the colossal magnetostriction effect and associated magnetic-field-induced structural phase transitions in rare-earth orthoferrites.
main_result: The single crystals exhibit unprecedentedly large, highly anisotropic magnetostriction (up to 100% along the c-axis) correlated with field-induced first-order structural transitions below the spin-reorientation temperature.
method: Measurements involved using a capacitive dilatometer to measure lattice strain ($\Delta l/l$) and magnetometers to measure magnetization ($M$) under varying magnetic fields and temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is single crystals of orthorhombic rare-earth orthoferrites, $	ext{RFeO}_3$ ($	ext{R} = 	ext{Dy}, 	ext{Ho}$), which are studied below their spin-reorientation transition temperature ($T_{SR}$).
key_observables: Magnetostriction ($s$), magnetodielectric effect ($\epsilon$), lattice strain ($\Delta l/l$), and magnetization ($M$) as functions of magnetic field ($H$) and temperature ($T$).
important_parameters: Magnetic fields up to 90 kOe; temperatures near the spin-reorientation transition ($T_{SR} \approx 50-55 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The colossal effects are attributed to a magnetic-field-induced first-order structural phase transition, possibly driven by large spin-orbit coupling and magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $M$ vs $T$ and $M$ vs $H$ loops, showing sharp transitions; $\Delta l/l$ vs $T$ curves demonstrating step-like changes in strain; and $s$ vs $H$ loops confirming large, hysteretic magnetostriction along the c-axis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements of magnetization, thermal expansion, and magnetostriction for $	ext{HoFeO}_3$ and $	ext{DyFeO}_3$, correlating the observed colossal strain and dielectric anomalies with magnetic phase transitions.
why_interesting: While primarily experimental, the study of field-induced structural transitions and the coupling between magnetic order and lattice strain touches upon concepts relevant to coupled order parameters and phase transitions studied in many-body physics.
